artifacts.value: Think of it like my F-150: Kelley Blue Book said it was worth $5k, but I sold it on payments for $12.5k because the buyer cared about the monthly, not the sticker. Your house is 'worth 40' to a cash buyer, but you want 100 — let me give you terms and you get your number.
We noticed your house went off market — what was your agent not able to get you that you were looking for?
You're behind / going through a divorce — we'll catch up your payments, put a couple grand in your hand, take over the payments and deed it to us. It's called subject-to. You down?
Instead of a 5-year balloon, let's turn this into a 50-year annuity for your son — when he's 62 he still gets a check every month. Turn this property into a memory you set up for him.
What does your life actually cost month to month — is it the $375 for the RV spot? Then let's set your payment right at that. The number serves you, not a spreadsheet.
The real question isn't 'why would the bank let you?' — it's 'why do I need the bank's permission to buy a house from a willing seller?' The seller and I can agree on terms directly.
